## ⚠️ Contradiction: Security deposit return deadline

- **§4.3, page 4:** "Landlord will return the Security Deposit, less lawful deductions, together with an itemized list of any deductions, within thirty (30) days after Tenant surrenders the Premises and returns all keys."
- **§26.3, page 19:** "The Security Deposit, less any lawful deductions, shall be returned within forty-five (45) days after the termination of this Lease."

These disagree on both the **deadline** (30 days vs. 45 days) and the **trigger event** (surrendering premises + returning keys, vs. lease termination — which are not necessarily the same date). The lease never says which one controls.

---

## Rent & payment (pages 2–3)

- **§3.2:** "Tenant shall pay monthly rent of one thousand six hundred fifty dollars ($1,650.00) ("Monthly Rent")."
- **§3.3:** "Monthly Rent is due in advance on the first (1st) day of each calendar month without demand. If the Commencement Date is not the first day of a month, rent for the first partial month shall be prorated on a daily basis **and paid before Tenant receives keys.**"
- **§3.7:** "A returned payment fee of thirty-five dollars ($35.00) is charged for each payment returned unpaid by a bank for any reason."
- **§3.8 (Late Charges):** "If Landlord has not received the full Monthly Rent by 11:59 p.m. on the fifth (5th) day of the month, Tenant shall pay an initial late charge of seventy-five dollars ($75.00), plus ten dollars ($10.00) for each additional day the rent remains unpaid, up to a maximum late charge of one hundred seventy-five dollars ($175.00) for that month." *(Deadline: rent must be received by 11:59 p.m. on the 5th.)*
- **§3.5** (relevant risk, not itself a fee): "Payments are applied first to unpaid fees and charges, then to past-due rent, then to current rent, regardless of any note written on the payment." — meaning a partial rent payment can leave you still "late" and generating more late fees under §3.8 if fees are owed.

## Security deposit (page 4)

- **§4.1:** "On or before signing this Lease, Tenant shall pay a security deposit of one thousand six hundred fifty dollars ($1,650.00)." *(Deadline: at/before signing.)*
- **§4.4:** "Lawful deductions include unpaid rent, unpaid fees, the cost of repairing damage beyond normal wear and tear, the cost of removing property or trash left in the Premises, and any other charge this Lease states may be deducted from the Security Deposit."
- See contradiction above (§4.3/§26.3) for the return deadline.

## Utilities (page 5)

- **§5.2:** "Tenant shall open accounts in Tenant's own name for electricity and gas effective on the Commencement Date... If service lapses and Landlord pays to restore it, Tenant shall repay Landlord **within ten (10) days** of a written request." *(Two deadlines: accounts active by Commencement Date; reimbursement within 10 days if landlord fronts it.)*
- **§5.3:** "Tenant shall keep the Premises heated to at least fifty-five degrees Fahrenheit (55°F) at all times from October 1 through April 30..." *(Ongoing seasonal obligation; failure could expose you to damage costs under §7.3.)*

- **§10.5:** "If a repair was made necessary by Tenant's misuse or neglect, Landlord will charge Tenant the reasonable cost of the repair."

- **§8.1:** "Tenant may end this Lease before the end of the Initial Term only by (a) giving Landlord written notice **at least sixty (60) days** before the date Tenant will move out, and (b) paying an early termination fee equal to **two (2) months' Monthly Rent** [$3,300]."
- **§8.2:** "The early termination fee is due with the notice. Rent remains due through the move-out date stated in the notice."
- **§8.4:** "If Tenant moves out without following Section 8.1, Tenant remains liable for rent through the end of the Initial Term, less any rent Landlord receives from a replacement tenant, plus Landlord's reasonable costs of re-renting."

## Insurance/liability exposure (page 9)

- **§11.3:** "Tenant shall indemnify Landlord against claims arising from the negligence of Tenant, occupants or guests in the Premises or the Common Areas." *(Open-ended potential cost.)*

## Notice timing mechanics (page 15)

- **§20.3:** "A notice sent by mail is effective three (3) days after mailing." — relevant to calculating whether you've met deadlines like the 60-day early-termination notice or 75-day non-renewal notice if you mail rather than hand-deliver/email/portal.

- **§21.1:** "Tenant may add notes to the report for **seven (7) days** after move-in." *(Deadline to dispute move-in condition.)*
- **§21.2:** "Tenant may request a pre-move-out inspection during the last **fourteen (14) days** of the Lease." *(Deadline/window.)*
- **§21.4:** "A carpet cleaning charge of **one hundred fifty dollars ($150.00)** will be deducted from the Security Deposit at move-out regardless of the condition of the carpet." *(Flat, unconditional fee.)*
- **§21.5:** "Keys not returned will be charged at the cost of rekeying the Premises."
- **§21.6:** "If Tenant leaves property behind after move-out... the cost will be deducted from the Security Deposit."
- **§21.7:** "If Tenant stays in the Premises after the Lease ends without Landlord's written consent, Tenant shall pay rent for each day of holdover at **one and one-half (1.5) times** the daily rate of the Monthly Rent, and is responsible for any losses Landlord suffers..."

## Casualty (page 17)

- **§22.3:** "If the casualty was caused by Tenant, occupants, guests or pets, rent does not abate and Tenant is responsible for the cost of repair to the extent not covered by Landlord's insurance."

## Alarms (page 17)

- **§23.3:** "Tenant shall pay for any fire department charge or damage resulting from Tenant disabling an alarm."

## Renewal & rent increase (page 18)

- **§25.1:** "This Lease will automatically renew for an additional term of twelve (12) months unless either party gives the other written notice of non-renewal **at least seventy-five (75) days** before the last day of the Initial Term." *(Critical deadline if you don't want to auto-renew.)*
- **§25.2:** "Landlord may increase the Monthly Rent for a renewal term by up to **six percent (6%)** by giving Tenant written notice of the new rent **at least ninety (90) days** before the last day of the current term."

## Overarching clause affecting all of the above (page 19)

- **§26.6:** "Time is of the essence for all payment and notice deadlines in this Lease." — this raises the stakes on every deadline listed above (e.g., the 60-day early-termination notice, the 75-day non-renewal notice, the 5th-of-month rent deadline).

---

**Bottom line:** Before signing, I'd get written clarification on the security-deposit conflict (§4.3 vs. §26.3) — ask which deadline and which trigger event actually applies, and get it in writing or an amendment, since §26.9 says the lease "may be changed only by a written amendment signed by Landlord and all Tenants."
